OpenCode Computer Use - full documentation summary
Canonical site: https://opencode-computer-use.pages.dev/
Repository: https://github.com/rashidtvmr/opencode-computer-use
License: MIT

1. What it is
OpenCode Computer Use is a dual-generation OpenCode plugin that provides a
Codex-style Computer Use session. Instead of exposing many low-level desktop
MCP tools, it exposes one persistent JavaScript surface through a local MCP
server named cua_repl. The model receives two tools only: js (evaluate
JavaScript in the persistent session) and js_reset (discard bindings and
start a clean session). App bindings and variables survive across model
turns. Native desktop calls are made by the underlying open-source
open-computer-use runtime (optional dependency open-computer-use@0.3.5),
kept separate from the Codex-style session adapter. The adapter is adapted
from the MIT-licensed iFurySt/open-codex-computer-use project; see
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in the repository.

2. Architecture (three layers)
- OpenCode plugin: loads the local package and registers cua_repl without
  exposing raw desktop tools.
- cua_repl MCP server: persistent JavaScript evaluation, output bounds,
  request validation, and worker isolation so a timed-out loop cannot wedge
  the server.
- Native runtime: open-computer-use runs as a separate child process. OS
  accessibility, screen capture, and input permissions are enforced there.
The JavaScript VM is a capability guard, not a complete security boundary.

3. Model workflow
The js tool accepts code (required JavaScript source), timeout_ms (optional,
capped at 300 seconds), and title (optional short action title).
Typical first call:
  var apps = await cua.listApps({ emit: false });
  var app = await cua.getApp(apps[0].id);
  await app.getAXState();
Typical action and verification:
  var save = await app.click(12);
  await app.getAXState();
State and action rules: read getAXState() or getAXStateAndScreenshot()
before acting on a new layout; element indexes belong to the most recent
state and must be re-derived after navigation, dialogs, scroll, resize, or
rerender; prefer element indexes and semantic actions over coordinates; use
coordinates only when no useful accessibility data exists; batch
deterministic actions with the next state read in one js call; never replay
a mutating action after a timeout or transport failure, observe again and
decide anew; js_reset discards JavaScript bindings only, not native app
state.

4. API
- cua.getState(options?): list current desktop apps with bounded output.
- cua.listApps(options?): structured app records without emitting by
  default.
- cua.getApp(nameOrPid): bind an app and emit initial accessibility state.
- app.getAXState(options?): fresh semantic accessibility tree.
- app.getScreenshot(options?): local image bytes, optionally emitted.
- app.getAXStateAndScreenshot(options?): combined state and image read.
- app.click(target, options?): element index first, bounded coordinate when
  necessary.
- app.scroll(elementIndex, direction, pages?)
- app.drag([fromX, fromY], [toX, toY])
- app.typeText(text)
- app.pressKey(key)
- app.setValue(elementIndex, value)
- app.performSecondaryAction(elementIndex, action)
- nodeRepl.write(value): extra bounded text output.
- nodeRepl.emitImage(bytesOrDataUrl): bounded local image output.

5. Options
backend (default auto: auto, native, or custom); command (required for
custom: fixed native MCP executable plus argv, no shell syntax); serverName
(default cua_repl); override (default false); safetyMode (default full, or
read-only to block mutating CUA methods and advertise read-only annotations);
appAccess (default allow all, with optional exact-name and ID allow/deny
rules); timeoutMs (default 30000); disabled (default false); maxTextChars
(default 200000); maxImageBytes (default 2097152);
allowGlobalPointerFallbacks (default false, off because it moves the real
pointer and changes focus; enable only for an explicit desktop automation
test where that input is intended). The proxy also reads matching
OPENCODE_COMPUTER_USE_* environment variables. Custom commands must implement
the native MCP operations used by cua: initialize, tools/list, tools/call,
and notifications.

6. Install
Published package:
  npm install @frontendxlab/opencode-computer-use
The package postinstall step detects OpenCode 1 versus OpenCode2 and local
versus global installation, edits JSONC without dropping comments, and is
idempotent. If both generations are ambiguous it makes no change and prints
manual instructions. Run it explicitly with npx opencode-computer-use-setup;
use --local, --global, --v1, or --v2 to choose explicitly. If pnpm reports
ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS, approve the package once with pnpm approve-builds
@frontendxlab/opencode-computer-use, or run pnpm exec
opencode-computer-use-setup manually. CI environments skip setup.
OpenCode 1 (opencode.json or opencode.jsonc, plugin list):
  { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
    "plugin": [["@frontendxlab/opencode-computer-use", { "backend": "auto" }]] }
OpenCode2 V2 (plugins shape):
  { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
    "plugins": [{ "package": "@frontendxlab/opencode-computer-use",
      "options": { "backend": "auto" } }] }
A local checkout can be used by replacing the package name with its absolute
path. Do not configure the same package both as an explicit plugin and through
automatic plugin discovery. If Node is not on PATH, set OPENCODE_NODE to an
absolute Node executable. Verify with: opencode mcp list.

7. Requirements and OS support
Requirements: Node.js 18 or newer; OpenCode 1.18.29 or newer (V1) or
OpenCode2 V2; a signed-in graphical desktop session; macOS Accessibility
and Screen Recording permissions; Linux AT-SPI plus required input and
capture services; Windows UI Automation in the interactive desktop session.
The plugin cannot control lock screens, login screens, UAC secure desktops,
or other OS-owned consent surfaces, and does not bypass permissions.
Packaged native targets: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64,
win32-arm64, win32-x64. Validation status: Linux x64 read-only discovery,
app listing, MCP registration, and persistent session passed local smoke
tests; one Ubuntu/GNOME Wayland session exposed a Chrome pseudo-window with
no actionable AT-SPI children and synthetic input did not change it (the
adapter reports the native result honestly); macOS and Windows have not
been live-tested in this environment and need on-host permission and
desktop validation.

8. Safety
High-privilege desktop-control surface. The js tool is marked conservatively
as mutating in full mode and read-only in read-only mode. The adapter also
bounds app bindings, sends native cancellation on timeouts, and sends a
best-effort turn-ended notification during shutdown. Keep OpenCode approval
prompts enabled for consequential actions (sending, deleting, purchasing,
uploading, changing permissions). Do not expose the session to an untrusted
model or run it unattended against password managers, banking, administrator,
or other high-value applications. Screenshots, accessibility trees, and typed
values can contain sensitive data and should stay local. Read SECURITY.md
before high-risk use. Manual read-only checks before acting:
  open-computer-use doctor
  open-computer-use list-apps

9. Troubleshooting (from the docs page)
- cua_repl not listed: check the active generation config, restart the TUI or
  background service after installation, run opencode mcp list, and avoid
  double registration. For global OpenCode2, run opencode2 plugin add
  @frontendxlab/opencode-computer-use if the package was installed before
  automatic setup was available.
- Node not found: set OPENCODE_NODE or fix server PATH.
- Empty app list: run open-computer-use list-apps in the same graphical
  session; confirm the app runs and desktop accessibility is available.
- Screenshots unavailable: OS compositor or permission gap; bounded
  accessibility text may still work.
- Linux input returns success but nothing changes: session type or missing
  runtime prerequisite; observe again before retrying mutating actions.
- Global pointer fallback rejected: expected safety gate.

10. WebMCP preview
The documentation page includes a progressive, read-only WebMCP enhancement
based on the current document.modelContext.registerTool draft. It registers
search_docs, get_install_config, and get_api_reference only when the browser
supports the API and the tools Permissions Policy. It does not expose desktop
control, shell, network mutation, or credentials. WebMCP is experimental and
should not be treated as stable browser support.

11. Development
npm install; npm test; npm run lint. Adapter tests use a fake native MCP
server and need no real desktop. Live desktop validation must run
separately per OS.
